activity_context.topic_title: Solving 2x2 Systems of Equations Using Inverse Matrices

examples.knowledge_point: Solving a 2x2 System of Equations Using an Inverse Matrix With Reorganization
examples.problem:
Solve the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}2x-3y=5 \\ 6y-5x=-8.\end{aligned}
$$
examples.worked_solution:
First, we reorganize the equations so that they are in the right order, to get

$$
{\begin{aligned}2x-3y=5 \\ -5x+6y=-8.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can represent this system of equations in the form $A\mathbf{x} =\mathbf{b}\mathbin{:}$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14052845/assets/240a1d2f7f93ec808127c9fa1791a77a43fcd7c0c84505540acc81c8b9fbc6e1.png)

To find the solution, we need to calculate the inverse of the coefficient matrix ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14052845/assets/7850cbafc78f2cf2ce14ae7111064bf2f5a029f4d1b97b6d5ebfc09e7126f44e.png) This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{6\cdot 2-3\cdot 5}[\begin{aligned}6 & 3 \\ 5 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =-\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}6 & 3 \\ 5 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

We can now find the solution to this system:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =-\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}6 & 3 \\ 5 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}5 \\ -8\end{aligned}] \\  & =-\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 9\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=-2$ and $y=-3.$

feedback.worked_solution:
This system can be written as

$$
[\begin{aligned}-4 & 2 \\ 1 & -3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

To find the solution, we need to calculate the inverse of the coefficient matrix 
$A=[\begin{aligned}-4 & 2 \\ 1 & -3\end{aligned}].$
This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{(-4)\cdot (-3)-1\cdot 2}[\begin{aligned}-3 & -2 \\ -1 & -4\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{10}[\begin{aligned}-3 & -2 \\ -1 & -4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

We can now represent the solution to this system as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =\frac{1}{10}[\begin{aligned}-3 & -2 \\ -1 & -4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
